plan.G: After the three research trees close, inspect their measured programs and evidence, including slower or incorrect attempts. Select only hypotheses supported by fresh correctness checks; combine complementary improvements cautiously because their gains may not be additive. Compile and check every integrated candidate afresh. Do not restart research or alter the protocol, target, compiler, checker, or protected host. Independently confirm the final candidate using the official confirmation procedure and keep the fastest correctly validated, independently confirmed program by geometric-mean CUDA-event time across N=4096, 8192, and 16384.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied kernel performs an O(N²) per-target source loop, making source reuse, a distinct source-parallel work mapping, and inner-loop instruction cost three useful, complementary opportunities. The baseline is reported valid and correct, with three search timing values and mean 0.00185436 s; there are no per-size timings or candidate measurements, so this does not establish which cost dominates. Keep hypotheses distinct and judge all candidates under the frozen correctness and timing protocol. Every tree must preserve complete output, the 28-byte Particle layout and kernel entry, the one-kernel interface, all stated edge cases and the oracle tolerances; it may edit only src/nbody_kernel.cu and src/launch.json.

children.objective: Develop a CTA source-tiled implementation focused on reusing each source particle across multiple target rows: cooperatively stage only the needed source fields in shared memory, synchronize safely, and handle incomplete source and target tiles. Initially keep the force arithmetic close to the reference to isolate the data-reuse change. Tune legal block, items_per_block, and shared_memory_bytes configurations. Respect grid.x=ceil(N/items_per_block): ensure every output row is written exactly once even when items_per_block differs from block. Preserve all required behavior, including self-exclusion, coincident positions, exact mass copying, and N=1. Report correctness and measured geometric-mean kernel time; do not change the harness or protocol.
children.subject: CTA shared-memory source tiling for one-thread-per-target work

children.objective: Explore a distinct warp-cooperative source-parallel mapping: lanes process different source particles for a target and combine partial force sums within the warp. Keep this line focused on parallelizing the source dimension rather than adding CTA shared-memory source tiling; assess the trade-off between shorter per-thread loops, reduction cost, and source traffic. Tune a legal block/items_per_block mapping that respects the fixed grid formula and writes each row exactly once, including tails and small N. Validate changed reduction order against the reference and independent FP64 oracle, all edge cases, and required tolerances; report measured geometric-mean kernel time.
children.subject: Warp-parallel source traversal with per-target partial reductions

children.objective: Explore instruction-level savings while retaining direct per-target source traversal: keep target state in registers, use explicit single-precision reciprocal-square-root where appropriate, and test the mathematically equivalent cancellation of the target-mass factor in acceleration. Treat the algebraic and approximate-math changes as hypotheses: preserve finite outputs, self-exclusion, update order, exact mass copying, and correctness for all specified inputs. Do not use global fast math or add shared-memory tiling or warp reductions in this line. Tune legal launch configuration while respecting the fixed grid formula and exact row coverage; report correctness and measured geometric-mean kernel time.
children.subject: Inner-loop arithmetic and reciprocal-square-root optimization
